hook.situation: A teammate is not sure whether a manager is still in a meeting, already left work, or can still reply. The goal is not to sound vague; it is to say your guess, condition, hope, or opinion at the right strength.
objectives: Use -ㄹ걸요 for a soft but fairly confident guess.
Use -다면 to open a hypothetical path before giving the next step.
Use 좋겠어요 and 것 같아요 to make wishes, suggestions, and opinions less blunt.
hook.whyItMatters: English learners often use one all-purpose 'I think...' for every uncertain sentence. Korean splits that work across several endings, so the listener can feel whether you are guessing, imagining a condition, hoping for an outcome, or politely softening your own opinion.

grammarNotes.title: -(으)ㄹ걸요 — A Soft but Confident Guess
grammarNotes.func: Use -(으)ㄹ걸요 when you make a guess you're fairly sure about, but want to sound gentle instead of flat-out telling someone. It feels like "I'd say..." or "probably..." based on what you know.

formTable.when: Verb/adjective stem ends in a vowel
Verb/adjective stem ends in a consonant

examples.en: My friend is probably home right now.
examples.note: A guess you're fairly sure of, softened so it doesn't sound like a flat claim.

examples.en: That movie's probably good.
examples.note: 있다 ends in a consonant, so it takes -을걸요.

examples.en: This book's probably a bit pricey.
examples.note: 비싸- ends in a vowel, so it takes -ㄹ걸요.

examples.en: My parents are probably asleep already.
examples.note: Uses the honorific 주무시다 (to sleep) for parents, while still keeping the guessing feel.

keyPoint.label: -(으)ㄹ걸요 vs. -(으)ㄹ 거예요
keyPoint.body: Both say something is likely. -(으)ㄹ 거예요 sounds like a plain prediction; -(으)ㄹ걸요 adds a softer "I'd guess" feeling, often when the other person might be thinking otherwise. Save the finer back-vowel rules for later — just match vowel vs. consonant stems for now.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 걸요 sounds like [거료], so 갈걸요 comes out [갈꺼료] — the ㄱ tenses and the ㄹ links smoothly into 요.

drill.instruction: Answer each question with a soft guess using -(으)ㄹ걸요.
drill.model: 친구 지금 뭐 해요? → 아마 자고 있을걸요.
items: 그 식당 지금 문 열었어요? → 아마 ___.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English speakers stack "probably" on top of another guess word. -(으)ㄹ걸요 already means "probably," so don't combine it with -(으)ㄹ 것 같다. Attach it straight to the plain stem: 올걸요.

grammarNotes.title: -(으)면 좋겠어요 — A Hope or Gentle Wish
grammarNotes.func: Use -(으)면 좋겠어요 to say "I hope..." or "I wish...". It literally means "it'd be nice if...," and it's the everyday way to say what you'd like to happen.

formTable.ex: 오다 → 오면 좋겠어요; 싸다 → 싸면 좋겠어요
먹다 → 먹으면 좋겠어요; 많다 → 많으면 좋겠어요

formTable.when: Wish about now / something not true
formTable.ex: 오다 → 왔으면 좋겠어요; 있다 → 있었으면 좋겠어요

examples.en: I hope the weather's nice tomorrow.
examples.note: A simple hope about the future; 좋다 ends in a consonant, so -으면.

examples.en: I wish I had a little more time.
examples.note: Everyday wish; 있다 takes -으면 좋겠어요.

examples.en: I hope this test is easy.
examples.note: The -었으면 form here makes the hope feel stronger, even though the test hasn't happened yet.

examples.en: I wish our place were closer to school.
examples.note: A wish about how things are now; 가깝다 is ㅂ-irregular, so 가까웠으면.

keyPoint.label: -(으)면 좋겠어요 vs. -고 싶어요
keyPoint.body: -고 싶어요 means "I want to (do it myself)." -(으)면 좋겠어요 means "I hope (it happens)," so it can be about other people, the weather, or things you don't control. The contrary-to-fact nuance of the -았/었으면 form gets fuller treatment in a later chapter.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 좋겠어요 sounds like [조케써요]: ㅎ + ㄱ blend into an aspirated [ㅋ], and 겠 tenses the next ㅅ into [써].

drill.instruction: Turn each situation into a wish using -(으)면 좋겠어요.
drill.model: 비가 와요. (싫어요) → 비가 안 오면 좋겠어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Don't slip 싶다 in. "I hope I go to Korea" is just 가면 좋겠어요. Adding 싶다 doubles the wanting and sounds off. Keep 가고 싶어요 for a plain "I want to go."

grammarNotes.title: -겠- — Intention, a Good Guess, or a Set Polite Phrase
grammarNotes.func: -겠- does three everyday jobs: stating your own plan ("I'll..."), making a guess about a situation ("that must be..."), and forming a few set polite phrases. You read which one it is from the context and the subject.

formTable.ex: 알겠어요 (got it); 모르겠어요 (I don't know); 잘 먹겠습니다

examples.en: I'll come back tomorrow.
examples.note: Your own plan; -겠습니다 sounds firm and polite, common when serving someone or in formal speech.

examples.en: This food looks so good!
examples.note: A guess from what you see — you haven't tasted it yet, but you can tell it must be good.

examples.en: That must have been rough with so much homework.
examples.note: -었겠어요 guesses about someone else's past and shows you feel for them.

examples.en: I don't really get what you mean.
examples.note: 모르겠어요 is a set, softened way to say it; plain 몰라요 can sound more blunt.

keyPoint.label: Intention -겠- vs. Guess -겠-
keyPoint.body: With "I" as the subject and an action verb, -겠- usually means a plan ("I'll"). With someone else, or with an adjective describing a situation, it means a guess ("must be / looks like"). The subject and the kind of verb tell you which. The polite "future" feel of -겠- in set phrases comes later.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: -겠- tenses the next consonant: 먹겠어요 → [먹께써요], 맛있겠어요 → [마싣께써요].

drill.instruction: Decide if it's a plan or a guess, then finish it with -겠-.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 그 사람 학생이에요? — said as 그 사람 학생이겠어요?
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Don't use -겠- for a plain yes/no question. -겠- adds "must be / I'm guessing," so 학생이겠어요? asks "I suppose he's a student?" To simply ask whether someone is a student, use 학생이에요?

grammarNotes.title: -다면 / N(이)라면 — If That Were the Case
grammarNotes.func: Use -다면 / N(이)라면 to set up a "what if" — an imagined or supposed situation, often one you don't really expect or that isn't true right now: "if (let's say)...".

examples.ko: 돈이 많다면 큰 집을 사고 싶어요.
examples.romanization: doni mantamyeon keun jibeul sago sipeoyo.
examples.en: If I had a lot of money, I'd want to buy a big house.
examples.note: A "what if" the speaker doesn't really expect; 많다 is an adjective, so -다면.

examples.ko: 내가 너라면 그 사람한테 전화할 거예요.
examples.romanization: naega neoramyeon geu saramhante jeonhwahal geoyeyo.
examples.en: If I were you, I'd call him.
examples.note: Noun + 라면 sets up an imagined "if I were" situation.

examples.en: If you happen to have time, let's catch a movie.
examples.note: 있다 takes -다면; here it frames a supposed condition before a suggestion.

examples.ko: 그때 일찍 출발했다면 안 늦었을 거예요.
examples.romanization: geuttae iljjik chulbalhaetdamyeon an neujeosseul geoyeyo.
examples.en: If we'd left early back then, we wouldn't have been late.
examples.note: -았/었다면 looks back at something that didn't happen — a regret about the past.

keyPoint.label: -다면 vs. -(으)면
keyPoint.body: -(으)면 is the all-purpose "if/when," fine for real, likely things (밥 먹으면 = when/if I eat). -다면 puts more weight on "just supposing," so it suits imagined or unlikely cases. For everyday real conditions, -(으)면 is still your default. The full -았/었다면 "would have" pattern is explored more later.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 많다면 sounds like [만타면]: the ㅎ in 많 blends with the following ㄷ into an aspirated [ㅌ].

drill.instruction: Make a "what if" sentence using -다면 / N(이)라면.
drill.model: (복권 당첨) 복권에 당첨된다면 여행을 갈 거예요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: After a noun, you can't just add -다면. Nouns use (이)라면: 학생이라면 (if you're a student), 부자라면 (if you're rich). Only verb and adjective stems take -다면 directly.

grammarNotes.title: -(으)ㄴ/는데요 — Softening and Leaving Room
grammarNotes.func: Ending a sentence with -(으)ㄴ/는데요 softens it. Instead of a hard statement, it sets something up and leaves the door open — for the other person to react, for a "but...," or for a gentle pushback. It's one of the most common ways Koreans avoid sounding too direct.

examples.en: I'm kind of busy right now... (so maybe later?)
examples.note: A soft "no" — it states the situation and lets the other person draw the conclusion, instead of flatly refusing.

examples.en: Um, this is my seat... (could you move?)
examples.note: Noun + 인데요 makes a gentle correction without sounding harsh.

examples.ko: 저는 매운 거 잘 못 먹는데요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun maeun geo jal mot meongneundeyo.
examples.en: I'm not so good with spicy food, actually...
examples.note: -는데요 softly raises a concern and leaves room for the other person to respond.

examples.en: It rained yesterday, though...
examples.note: Past -았/었는데요 gently offers a fact, often hinting at a "but" the listener can pick up on.

keyPoint.label: -(으)ㄴ/는데요 vs. a plain -아/어요 ending
keyPoint.body: 좀 바빠요 just states "I'm busy." 좀 바쁜데요 says the same thing but trails off, inviting the other person to fill in the rest — softer and less final. Use it to hedge, hint, or set up a contrast. Its longer use for connecting two clauses ("~는데, …") comes in a separate point.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In 먹는데요, the ㄱ before ㄴ turns nasal: it sounds like [멍는데요]. 좋은데요 sounds like [조은데요], with the ㅎ dropping out.

drill.instruction: Soften each blunt sentence by re-ending it with -(으)ㄴ/는데요.
items: 저는 그 영화 별로예요. → 저는 그 영화 ___.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 저 지금 바쁜데요 그래서 못 가요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 저 지금 바쁜데요. (and let the meaning land on its own)
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English speakers spell out the whole "so I can't go." The point of -(으)ㄴ/는데요 is to leave that part unsaid and let the listener get it. Tacking on the blunt conclusion undoes the softening the ending is there to create.

exampleSentence.en: They are probably still in a meeting.

extendedVocabulary.english: I hope; it would be good if...

exampleSentence.en: It would be good to leave a message.

exampleSentence.ko: 혹시 이미 나갔다면 메시지를 남겨 두면 좋겠어요.
exampleSentence.en: If they already left, it would be good to leave a message.

exampleSentence.ko: 제 생각에는 먼저 물어보는 게 좋을 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: In my opinion, I think it would be good to ask first.
I will ask carefully.
Since I am not sure, I will ask carefully.
The person in charge probably knows.
Hmm, they may have already left work.

exampleSentence.ko: 제 생각에는 먼저 물어보는 게 좋을 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: In my opinion, I think it would be good to ask first.
It would be good to state the opinion carefully.
Since I am not sure, I will ask carefully.

exampleSentence.ko: 이렇게 말하면 좀 부담스러운 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: If we say it this way, I think it feels a bit pressuring.

exampleSentence.ko: 혹시 이미 나갔다면 메시지를 남겨 두면 좋겠어요.
exampleSentence.en: If they already left, it would be good to leave a message.
They may have already left work.
They are probably still in a meeting.
They are probably still in a meeting.
It would be good to leave a message.
They may have already left work.

extendedVocabulary.english: to ask; to ask and find out

exampleSentence.en: Since I am not sure, I will ask carefully.
I think there is also a possibility of that.

exampleSentence.ko: 확실하지 않을 때는 너무 단정하지 말고 조심스럽게 추측해요.
exampleSentence.en: When you are not sure, do not state it too firmly; guess carefully.

extendedDialogue.setting: Two coworkers need to contact someone, but they are not sure whether that person is still available.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: They are probably still in a meeting.
lines.grammarNote: -ㄹ걸요 gives a soft but fairly confident guess.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Hmm, they may have already left work.
lines.grammarNote: 글쎄요 and 수도 있어요 keep the uncertainty open.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 혹시 이미 나갔다면 메시지를 남겨 두면 좋겠어요.
lines.romanization: hoksi imi nagatdamyeon mesijireul namgyeo dumyeon jokesseoyo.
lines.en: If they already left, it would be good to leave a message.
lines.grammarNote: -다면 opens the hypothetical; -으면 좋겠어요 gives a gentle next step.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Yes, since I am not sure, I will ask carefully.
lines.grammarNote: 조심스럽게 controls tone, not just grammar.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 제 생각에는 먼저 물어보는 게 좋을 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: je saenggageneun meonjeo mureoboneun ge joeul geot gatayo.
lines.en: In my opinion, I think it would be good to ask first.
lines.grammarNote: 제 생각에는 plus 것 같아요 softens the opinion.

readingText.title: 확실하지 않을 때 말하는 법
readingText.body: 회사 단톡방에서 누가 아직 회의 중인지, 이미 퇴근했는지 모를 때가 있어요. 이때 한국어는 한 가지 'I think'만 쓰지 않아요. 기억이나 상황을 보고 짐작하면 '아직 회의 중일걸요'라고 말할 수 있고, 가능성을 열어 두고 싶으면 '이미 나갔다면 메시지를 남겨 두면 좋겠어요'처럼 말해요. 내 의견을 조심스럽게 말할 때는 '제 생각에는 먼저 물어보는 게 좋을 것 같아요'가 자연스러워요. 중요한 건 약하게 말하는 것이 아니라, 내가 아는 정도에 맞게 문장을 고르는 거예요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: In a work chat, you may not know whether someone is still in a meeting or already left work. Korean does not use one single 'I think' for every case. Use -ㄹ걸요 for a hunch, -다면 for a hypothetical, 좋겠어요 for a hoped-for or gentle next step, and 것 같아요 to soften your own opinion. The point is not to be weak; it is to match the sentence to how much you actually know.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 회의 중인지 확실하지 않을 때 어떤 표현을 쓸 수 있어요?
이미 나갔을 가능성을 열어 둘 때 어떤 연결을 썼어요?
내 의견을 조심스럽게 말할 때 왜 것 같아요를 써요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 의견을 너무 단정적으로 들리지 않게 부드럽게 만들기 위해서예요.

culturalNote.title: Soft does not mean unclear
culturalNote.body: Korean hedging is often about social accuracy. If you are guessing, your ending should sound like a guess. If you are giving advice, the sentence should leave room for the listener. This is why 아마, 글쎄요, 혹시, 제 생각에는, -ㄹ걸요, -다면, 좋겠어요, and 것 같아요 often appear together in workplace chats, group projects, and polite disagreement.
culturalNote.tip: Before speaking, ask: am I guessing, imagining a condition, hoping for a result, or giving an opinion? Then choose the ending that matches that job.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence gives a soft but fairly confident guess?
inlineExercises.explanation: -ㄹ걸요 marks a careful guess based on what the speaker thinks.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence opens a hypothetical before suggesting the next step?
options: 이미 나갔다면 메시지를 남겨 두면 좋겠어요.
이미 나간 것 같아요 회의 중이에요.
inlineExercises.correct: 이미 나갔다면 메시지를 남겨 두면 좋겠어요.
inlineExercises.explanation: -다면 sets up the condition, and -으면 좋겠어요 gives a gentle suggestion.

inlineExercises.prompt: Soften this opinion: 제 생각에는 먼저 물어보는 게 좋을 ____.
inlineExercises.explanation: 좋을 것 같아요 softens the whole opinion. 같아요 alone would not attach correctly here.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which reply is the standard, fixed way to say you understood a request?
inlineExercises.explanation: 알겠어요 is a set response meaning 'I understand / okay.'

inlineExercises.prompt: 제 생각___ 먼저 물어보는 게 좋아요. (In my opinion...)
inlineExercises.explanation: 제 생각에는 frames the statement as your opinion. 을 and 에서 do not make the opinion-frame expression.

inlineExercises.prompt: 회의 자료는 아직 회의실에 ___ . (있다 → soft confident guess)
inlineExercises.explanation: -(으)ㄹ걸요 gives a soft but fairly confident guess. 있다 becomes 있을걸요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'If that is the case, let's ask first.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 그렇다면 opens a hypothetical path from the previous idea. 먼저 물어봐요 gives the suggested next step.
-면 좋겠어요 expresses a hope or gentle wish. 잘되면 sets the hoped-for condition.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence if you mean a wish: '잘될걸요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 잘될걸요 is a guess that it will probably go well. 잘되면 좋겠어요 is the wish: I hope it goes well.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which response is the cautious “Hmm, I am not sure”?
inlineExercises.explanation: 글쎄요 is the natural cautious hesitation. 좋겠어요 is a wish, and 그렇다면요 depends on a hypothetical.

bullets: -ㄹ걸요: a hunch or careful guess, as in 아직 회의 중일걸요.
-다면: a hypothetical condition, as in 이미 나갔다면.
좋겠어요: a hoped-for result or gentle suggestion, as in 메시지를 남겨 두면 좋겠어요.
것 같아요: a softened impression or opinion, not 같다 meaning 'same.'
-겠-: context decides the meaning: 알겠어요, 물어보겠습니다, 피곤하시겠어요.

writingTask.prompt: Answer a coworker who asks whether the boss will approve the plan: give a soft, confident guess, then add what you'd personally hope happens.
writingTask.hint: Make a gentle guess with -(으)ㄹ걸요 (괜찮을걸요) and -겠- or 것 같아요, express a wish with -(으)면 좋겠어요 (괜찮으면 좋겠어요), and soften the whole reply with trailing -(으)ㄴ/는데요.
writingTask.model: 글쎄요, 아마 부장님이 괜찮다고 하실걸요. 제 생각에는 큰 문제는 없을 것 같은데요. 그래도 다들 부담 없이 받아들이면 좋겠어요. 내일이면 확실히 알 수 있겠죠.
writingTask.modelEn: Hmm, the manager will probably say it's fine, I'd guess. In my opinion there shouldn't be a big problem, though. Still, I hope everyone takes it without feeling pressured. By tomorrow we'll surely know for sure.

canDo: Offer a soft but confident guess with -(으)ㄹ걸요 (괜찮을걸요)
Express a hope or wish with -(으)면 좋겠어요 (괜찮으면 좋겠어요)
Read -겠- as intention, a guess, or a set phrase (알 수 있겠죠)
Hedge and leave room with trailing -(으)ㄴ/는데요 and 아마 / 글쎄요
